- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply slight upward bias for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
- Model overestimates in late horizon (15–30 days) — apply downward bias, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, model tends to overpredict; if below, underpredict — adjust toward recent 10-day average.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag — forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of true reversal.
